app.name: Microsoft Outlook (Microsoft Graph via Microsoft Entra ID)

verdict.summary: Prototyping is easy: Composio's managed Outlook OAuth app works now with no registration. Your own Entra app is also self-serve, but the broad default scope set, tenant consent settings, and unverified multitenant limits make a production rollout to other organisations harder.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 45-90 min for your own Entra app and first connection; 2-4 hours more to trim scopes, test with a second user, and prepare publisher verification if you want it
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 20-30 min after you create the Entra app
verdict.approval_wait: None documented for connecting your own account or for unverified use in your own tenant. No published wait for publisher verification; the source says it can take minutes for an organisation that already meets the prerequisites.

gates.name: Your own account (single developer)
gates.unlocks: Create the Entra app and connect your own Microsoft account to it, through Composio or your own code.
limits: Authorization codes expire after about 1 minute, so exchange them promptly.
Access tokens in Microsoft's example last about 3599 seconds (about 1 hour).
Refresh tokens are issued only if offline_access is requested, and they are long-lived.

gates.name: Unverified multitenant app (users in your tenant and other tenants, no publisher verification)
gates.unlocks: Standard users in your own tenant can connect once tenant consent allows it. Users in other tenants can consent only if the app requests basic permissions, or if risk-based step-up consent is off.
limits: If user consent is disabled or restricted in the tenant, standard users are blocked even when admin consent was granted.
With risk-based step-up consent enabled, other-tenant users cannot consent to unverified multitenant apps that request more than basic sign-in and profile permissions; they see a warning instead.
No Microsoft-stated user or install caps for unverified apps were found.
Graph throttles apply: a global limit of 130,000 requests per 10 seconds per app across all tenants; a community-reported per-mailbox limit of 10,000 requests per 10 minutes.
gates.time_to_reach: Same day, once tenant consent settings are checked

gates.name: Publisher-verified app (Microsoft publisher verification)
gates.unlocks: A verified publisher name on the consent prompt, and the ability to clear the step-up consent block for other-tenant users (per the blocker finding). Use this when you need broad, public use.
limits: Requires a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that is the partner global account (PGA) for your organisation; location Partner IDs are not supported.
Requires a Microsoft Entra work or school tenant with a publisher domain. Personal Microsoft accounts cannot be verified, and the domain cannot be *.onmicrosoft.com.
Not supported for apps in national-cloud tenants.
No charge and no license required.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes if prerequisites are already in place; no published wait time was found

steps.title: Prototype on Composio's managed Outlook config
steps.detail: In Composio, connect an Outlook account using the managed OAuth config for the outlook toolkit. This needs no Entra app and is the fastest way to confirm your agent's calls work. Expect the broad default scope set.
gotchas: Composio's default scopes are broad. Expect consent prompts for mail send, chat and mailbox settings.

steps.title: Create the Entra app registration
steps.detail: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center and go to App registrations, then choose New registration. Give the app a name. Choose the supported account types for your audience (work/school, personal Microsoft accounts, or both). You can leave the redirect URI blank on this screen and add it in the next step.
gotchas: The exact wording of the account-type options was not verified from a Microsoft page. Check it on the screen.
Personal-account (Outlook.com) audiences cannot later be publisher-verified.

steps.title: Add the Redirect URI on a web platform
steps.detail: Open the app's authentication settings and add a redirect URI. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. The value must match exactly, and it is URL-encoded in the authorize request. For production, use HTTPS.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Platform (to confirm)
values.value: Web (server-side callback). Confirm with Composio that its callback expects a confidential client.

gotchas: A mismatch between the registered and sent redirect URI is a common failure.
Native apps should use https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/nativeclient (embedded browser) or http://localhost (system browser). Composio's flow is not a native app.

steps.title: Add a credential for the web platform
steps.detail: Create a client secret or certificate for the app. Confidential web apps need one of these when redeeming the code. Copy the secret value when it is shown, because you cannot read it again later. Do not add a secret if you choose a public (SPA or native) platform.
gotchas: The menu label for credentials was not verified from a Microsoft page.

steps.title: Add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions
steps.detail: Open API permissions, add a permission, choose Microsoft Graph, then choose Delegated permissions. Start with the smallest set you need. A minimum for mail reading with refresh is Mail.Read, User.Read and offline_access. Add more only when a feature requires it.
gotchas: Do not copy Composio's full default list into your app without deciding which scopes you need.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in Composio and connect your own account
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom auth config for Outlook. Enter the Application (client) ID and the secret or certificate from your Entra app. Then connect your own Microsoft account. Confirm a refresh token is returned.

values.label: Client ID
values.value: Application (client) ID from the Entra app overview

gotchas: Use the common endpoints only if your audience matches the account types you selected. The 'common' authority accepts both work and personal accounts.
Authorization codes expire in about 1 minute; the exchange must happen promptly.

steps.title: Check Microsoft Graph responses against a standard user
steps.detail: Have an agent run one authorization and one token refresh for a standard (non-admin) user in your tenant, then one calendar read and one mail read. Record any consent error text. A not-authorized-to-consent error means the scope needs an administrator.

steps.title: Check tenant user-consent settings
steps.detail: If standard users cannot consent, an administrator must change the tenant's user-consent settings in Entra (for example, to allow consent for low-impact permissions, or to grant admin consent for the app). Admin consent does not help if user consent is disabled or restricted.
gotchas: Admin consent granted for the app does not unblock standard users if user consent is disabled or restricted in the tenant.

steps.title: Trim the scope list to what the agent actually uses
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to the scopes it needs. Remove write and send scopes (Mail.Send, Chat.ReadWrite, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite, Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared, Contacts.ReadWrite) unless a feature needs them. Each removed scope lowers the consent friction for users and admins.
gotchas: The default low-impact set in one community source does not include Mail.Send. Do not assume a scope will consent without testing it.

steps.title: Confirm which scopes need admin consent
steps.detail: Test each remaining scope with a standard user in a tenant that has user consent restricted. Record which ones fail. Only Mail.Read (delegated) has been confirmed as not requiring admin consent. Check each other scope against Microsoft's permissions reference before you ship.

steps.title: Check publisher verification prerequisites
steps.detail: Confirm that your organisation has a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that is its partner global account. Confirm that the app is in a work or school tenant with a publisher domain (not *.onmicrosoft.com). Confirm the CPP account's email domain matches the publisher domain or a DNS-verified custom domain. Confirm your tenant is not a national cloud.
gotchas: The app must be in a work or school tenant. A personal-account app cannot be verified.
Publisher verification is not supported in national-cloud tenants.

steps.title: Run publisher verification
steps.detail: Sign in with Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication as a user with an Entra application administrator role and a CPP partner admin role. Start publisher verification for the app. The Entra portal location for this step was not verified; check Microsoft's publisher verification documentation.
gotchas: Microsoft does not charge for verification.

steps.title: Handle Graph throttling in the agent
steps.detail: Build retry logic that honours HTTP 429 and the Retry-After header. Plan for the global app limit and the lower per-mailbox limit that a community source reports. Confirm the per-mailbox number against Microsoft's throttling page before relying on it.
gotchas: The 10,000 per 10 minutes per-mailbox limit comes from a community source, not the official page.

steps.title: Check the message-property change date before shipping write features
steps.detail: If the agent edits sensitive properties of delivered (non-draft) messages, check Microsoft's announcement for the change dated December 31, 2026. A community report says these edits will need elevated Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite-type permissions with admin consent.
gotchas: The date is from a community blog. Verify it against Microsoft before treating it as an obligation.

requirements.item: Redirect URI exactly matches the registered value
requirements.detail: The redirect URI in the authorize request must exactly match one registered in Entra, URL-encoded.

requirements.item: Client secret or certificate for confidential web apps
requirements.detail: Web (confidential) apps need a client secret or certificate when redeeming codes. Public clients (SPA, native) must not send one.
Microsoft recommends PKCE for all application types and requires it for SPAs using the auth code flow.
Refresh tokens are returned only if offline_access is requested.

requirements.item: Tenant user-consent settings allow standard users
requirements.detail: If user consent is disabled or restricted, standard users cannot connect even with admin consent.

requirements.item: Publisher verification: CPP partner global account
requirements.detail: Must be a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that is the partner global account for the developer's organisation. Location Partner IDs are not supported.

requirements.item: Publisher verification: work or school tenant with a publisher domain
requirements.detail: Personal-account apps cannot be verified; the publisher domain cannot be *.onmicrosoft.com.
The verifying user needs an Entra application administrator role and a CPP partner admin role, and must sign in with Entra MFA.
Apps in national-cloud tenants cannot be publisher verified at this time.

scopes.effect: Lets the app read the signed-in user's mailbox. Not flagged as needing admin consent; the application (all-mailbox) form does. Consentable in personal Microsoft accounts.
Needed for refresh tokens. Included in the low-impact default set in a community source.

Write access to mail. Admin-consent status was not confirmed. A community report says edits to sensitive properties of delivered messages will need Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite-type permissions with admin consent from Dec 31, 2026.
Sends mail as the user. Not in the community low-impact default set, so expect it may need user or admin consent. Confirm by testing.
A community answer advises assuming Teams chat and meeting content permissions may need admin consent.
Calendar read and write. Admin-consent status was not confirmed individually. Community guidance says Exchange mailbox data permissions may need admin consent.
Mailbox settings access. Admin-consent status was not confirmed.
Contacts write access. Admin-consent status was not confirmed.
Reads the signed-in user's basic profile. Admin-consent status was not confirmed individually.

blockers.symptom: Authorize request fails with a redirect URI mismatch error
blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent does not exactly match a URI registered in the Entra app, or it is not URL-encoded.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact Composio callback URL into the app's redirect URI list and make sure the value matches character for character.

blockers.symptom: Standard user gets a not-authorized-to-consent error or cannot connect
blockers.cause: The scope is admin-restricted, or the tenant's user-consent settings are disabled or restricted.
blockers.fix: Ask a tenant administrator to grant consent or to change the tenant's user-consent settings in Entra. Trim the scope set so the request needs fewer admin-restricted permissions.

blockers.symptom: Users in other tenants see a warning and cannot consent
blockers.cause: Risk-based step-up consent is enabled, and the app is multitenant, not publisher verified, and requests more than basic sign-in and profile permissions.
blockers.fix: Reduce the request to basic permissions, or complete publisher verification from a work or school tenant.

blockers.symptom: Publisher verification cannot start on a personal-account app
blockers.cause: Apps registered with a Microsoft account cannot be publisher verified.
blockers.fix: Register the app in a Microsoft Entra work or school tenant with a publisher domain.

blockers.symptom: Publisher verification is unavailable in the tenant
blockers.cause: The tenant is a national-cloud tenant, which is not supported.
blockers.fix: Use a commercial-cloud tenant. National-cloud apps cannot be verified at this time.

blockers.cause: The app exceeded a Graph throttle: the global per-app limit or, per a community report, the per-mailbox limit.
blockers.fix: Honour the Retry-After header, back off, and reduce request volume per mailbox.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Outlook config to prototype; it needs no Entra app. Move to your own Entra app when you need your own branding, your own redirect URI, publisher verification, or a scope set you control. Composio's default scope list is broad (it includes Mail.Send, Chat.ReadWrite and MailboxSettings.ReadWrite), and some of those may need admin consent or be blocked in restricted tenants. Trim the list in your own app.

evidence.quote: Navigate to Azure Portal > App registrations > New registration.

evidence.quote: The *Mail.Read* delegated permission is available for consent in personal Microsoft accounts.

evidence.quote: Starting December 31, 2026, modifying sensitive properties on non-draft messages requires one of the following elevated permissions.

evidence.claim: A tenant can restrict user consent to low-impact permissions; a community blog gives the default low-impact set as openid, profile, email and offline_access, which excludes Mail.Send.
evidence.quote: the default low-impact set is openid, profile, email and offline_access.

evidence.claim: Publisher verification requires a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that is the partner global account for the developer's organisation; location Partner IDs are not supported.
evidence.quote: The CPP account must be the partner global account (PGA) for the developer's organization.

evidence.claim: Publisher verification needs an Entra work or school tenant with a publisher domain. Personal-account apps cannot be verified; the publisher domain cannot be *.onmicrosoft.com.
evidence.quote: Apps that are registered by using a Microsoft account can't be publisher verified.

evidence.claim: The CPP account email domain must match the publisher domain or a DNS-verified custom domain. The verifying user needs an Entra application administrator role and a CPP partner admin role, and must sign in with MFA.
evidence.quote: The user who initiates verification must sign in by using Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication.

evidence.claim: Microsoft does not charge developers for publisher verification and no license is required; developers who already meet prerequisites can be verified in minutes.
evidence.quote: Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification.

evidence.claim: Publisher verification is not supported for apps in national-cloud tenants.
evidence.quote: Apps that are registered in national cloud tenants can't be publisher verified at this time.

evidence.quote: users can't consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that *aren't* publisher verified.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Graph imposes a global per-app limit across all tenants of 130,000 requests per 10 seconds; service-specific limits sit on top.
evidence.quote: 130,000 requests per 10 seconds

evidence.quote: Use Single-page application (SPA) for client-side flows (auto-enables PKCE).

evidence.claim: Graph app registration docs say the redirect URI can be left empty on the first screen and configured afterwards under platform settings.
evidence.quote: You'll configure a redirect URI in the next section.

evidence.claim: A community guide adds Graph permissions under API permissions by choosing Microsoft Graph and then Delegated permissions.
evidence.quote: select **Microsoft Graph**, then **Delegated permissions**.

evidence.claim: The Composio default scope set includes sending and chat write scopes, some of which may need admin approval or be blocked in restricted tenants. Trim the scope list in your own app.

open_questions: Exact Entra UI wording for account types (work/school versus personal Microsoft accounts) was not verified from a Microsoft page. The authority choice (common, organizations, consumers) is from the official doc.

Whether Composio's callback URL must be entered as the redirect URI in a customer-owned Entra app was not verified. Composio's default redirect (backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) differs from the callback path seen in the probe (api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). Confirm in Composio's docs.
Whether Composio's flow is confidential (needs a client secret, Web platform) or public (SPA/native, no secret) was not verified. This decides the platform and credential steps.

Per-scope admin-consent flags for Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, Calendars, Chat, MailboxSettings, Contacts and User.Read were not individually confirmed. Only Mail.Read delegated and application were confirmed.
No Microsoft-stated user-count or install caps for unverified multitenant apps were found. Per-app Graph throttles are the only confirmed numeric limits.
The Outlook per-mailbox throttle (10,000 per 10 minutes) comes only from community sources. Verify against Microsoft's throttling page.
The Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite change date (December 31, 2026) comes from a community blog. Verify against Microsoft's own announcement; it is about two months from today.
No timeline beyond 'verified in minutes' was found for publisher verification. Whether a Microsoft review step follows submission was not confirmed.
Exact Entra portal navigation (Authentication blade, credentials section, publisher domain/branding blade) comes from community sources, not fetched Microsoft pages.
